Bottomless
bŏt´tum-les
adj. (without floor; rendering Greek abussos)
Bottom with the privative ending. The Greek abussos gives us abyss — a depth with no measurable floor.

Biblical Definition

Bottomless describes the abyss. Revelation gives it a key and a keeper: “there was given unto him the key of the bottomless pit” (Rev 9:1), and later an angel comes down “having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand” to bind the dragon (Rev 20:1–3). The beast ascends out of it (Rev 11:7), and Paul uses the same word of the deep: “Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead)” (Rom 10:7).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines bottomless as without a bottom; having no bottom; fathomless.

expand to see more

BOTTOMLESS, a. Without a bottom; having no bottom; fathomless.

Key Scripture

Rev 9:1 — "And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit."

Rev 20:1 — "And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand."

Rev 11:7 — "And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them."

Rom 10:7 — "Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)"

Modern Corruption

Evil is imagined as either mythological or merely psychological, and Revelation describes a place with a key — held, and not by the powers inside it.

expand to see more

The recurring detail in Revelation is the key. The bottomless pit is never described as open by its own power; something is given a key, or an angel comes down having the key and a great chain. Whatever is in the abyss is contained, and the containment is administered from outside. That single structural fact governs how a Christian should read every account of evil's activity in history.

Revelation 20:1-3 presses it further: the angel laid hold on the dragon… and bound him a thousand years, and cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him. Four verbs of restraint in one sentence. The abyss is bottomless from the inside; from above it has a lid, a lock, and a seal.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek abussos (G12), bottomless, the abyss — also the Septuagint's word for the deep of Genesis 1:2.

expand to see more

Greek abussos (G12) — bottomless pit, abyss; Revelation 9:1-11, 11:7, 17:8, 20:1-3, Luke 8:31.

Greek kleis (G2807) — key; Revelation 9:1, 20:1, and 1:18, I have the keys of hell and of death.

Greek halusis (G254) — chain; Revelation 20:1.

Usage

"“The key of the bottomless pit” — held, and not from inside."

"“Bound him… shut him up, and set a seal upon him” — four verbs of restraint."

"“Who shall descend into the deep?” — Paul's rhetorical impossibility."
